dedupe_keys.name: coal mine plans collection mining remediation authority

description: The Mining Remediation Authority holds more than 120,000 coal mine plans for Great Britain, dating back to the 17th century, covering both surface (opencast) and deep mining. The plans show areas of coal extraction in one or more seams at the time each plan was drawn and the points of entry into the seam, with mine entries (shafts and adits) drawn in varied symbols; a guide explains how to read them and warns that mine entries can be confused with surface features such as wells and chimneys. The collection is presented through the Authority's map viewer, with a PDF guide "Understanding coal mine plans". The licence field reads "Licence not specified" and the image formats are not stated on the page read; the entry was added in March 2026. Caveats: plans are historical drawings of varying accuracy and legends, and turning them into usable data needs interpretation. For simulation it is the primary evidence of where coal was worked, used to map shallow workings and mine entries under present roads, railways, pipelines and buildings. Related catalogue records include the Development High Risk Area and BGS Mining Hazard (not including coal).
